newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures close lower on currency, tender.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures close lower on currency, tender.

text.p: A strong pound after Wednesday's increase in the UK minimum lending rate continued to put pressure UK grain futures on Thursday.
Traders said the weekly European Union grain tender was also a factor.
The EU granted export licences for 233,700 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at 19.98 Ecus and sold just 1,000 tonnes of barley at 30.99 Ecus.
"People would have been looking for around 300,000 tonnes of wheat and 1,000 tonnes of barley is just a joke," said one trader.
At the close wheat futures were 0.75 to 1.10 stg down on a turnover of 600 lots while barley was 0.25 stg down after trading 129 lots.
In Amsterdam the milling wheat futures contract was neglected.
Lower grain futures were good news for the cash market with delivered traders reporting an active day.
"Tonnages have been high and there is a feeling that farmers are begining to panic because they now feel they have missed the boat following the recent sharp fall in prices," said a trader.
Nearby feed wheat in East Anglia was fetching 100 stg a tonne while new crop (1997) was trading from 97 down to 96 stg a tonne.
On the fob market Jan/Mar feed wheat fetched 101.75 stg a tonne and Apr/Jun 102.50 stg fob east coast ports.
